messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: Multiple OOMs + CUDA errors observed on runtime-gpu-eu-west-*. Group: runtime-paged-kv. Autoscaling not keeping up. Paging + slow mem creep suspected. Alert spike started ~1799991200.

maya (oncall): I'm taking this. pulling metrics now.

maya (oncall): quick summary from alert page: 8/12 pods in pool are reporting OOMKilled in last 10m, 5 show repeated `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`. Latency spikes for customers A and C.

henry (runtime): copying logs from one affected pod:
```
[2026-03-15T03:07:12Z] runtime: kv_cache: slab_alloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T03:07:12Z] runtime: attention_pager: page-resident count high -> eviction unable to make progress
[2026-03-15T03:07:12Z] cuda: driver reported CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS at 0x7f9a...
[2026-03-15T03:07:12Z] container: OOMKilled (OOM score 1000)
```
henry (runtime): pattern looks like fragmentation + slow KV slab drift where free lists are not reclaiming small fragments, slow creep until OOM.

lia (sre): triage checklist: reduce concurrency, enable aggressive eviction, cordon bad nodes, start warm standby.

maya (oncall): doing quick mitigations: 1) toning down per-pod concurrency to 4 2) lowering max_seq_len in runtime config for canary 3) scale up dedicated pool by +2 nodes (if infra agrees)

sam (infra): scaling up now, spinning two additional g4dn-equivalent nodes into the pool. ETA ~90s. Also increasing kube eviction thresholds temporarily.

emily (support): customer-impact: two customers hit tail latency >5s and a small % of requests failed with 503; we've opened support tickets for both and added status note.

maya (oncall): doing rolling restart on most impacted pods to clear per-process KV fragmentation; will keep one pod with old config as canary.

k8s-bot: kubectl rollout restart daemonset/runtime-worker -n runtime returned: started restart of 6 pods

henry (runtime): quick hotfix we can toggle: enable "kv_slab_compact_on_free" (cheap path) and bump eviction aggressiveness. Config snippet:
```yaml
runtime:
  kv_cache:
    slab_compaction: on_free
    compaction_interval_s: 30
    eviction_target_free_ratio: 0.18
    max_concurrent_requests: 4
```
henry (runtime): I can roll that to the canary pod now, then to rest after 5m monitoring.

maya (oncall): canary roll with slab_compaction on. Observing metrics.

lia (sre): also recommend turning off attention paging for long sequences on the canary to avoid kernel-level scatter. Set `attention_paging: disabled` for canary route.

maya (oncall): applied to canary. tracing + pprof on.

henry (runtime): early telemetry: canary shows memory plateau and no further CUDA errors in the last 60s. Eviction rate up 2x, compaction running.

maya (oncall): rolling the config to remaining pods with staggered restart (30s interval) to avoid cascade.

sam (infra): new nodes are in and accepting pods. Kube node pressure cleared on two nodes.

emily (support): I updated status page: "Investigating increased error rates and latency in EU region; mitigation underway." Customers notified via support cases.

lia (sre): note for postmortem: collect tcmalloc/malloc_stats, slab free list histograms, and allocation backtraces for affected processes. We'll need to correlate compaction metrics with tail-latency.

henry (runtime): also capture GPU coredumps from any container that raised `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`. Might be related to stale KV pointers crossing to attention pager path under fragmentation.

maya (oncall): after rolling restarts + compaction toggle + extra nodes, OOMs have dropped to 1/12 pods in last 10m. CUDA errors gone. Latency improving.

emily (support): customers A and C acknowledged mitigation, scaling-related transient errors. They asked for RCA and ETA for permanent fix.

lia (sre): set post-incident actions: 1) force compaction default for paged-kv pools 2) add evict-on-threshold periodic job 3) build regression test that simulates slow allocation creep under heavy seq_len/kv mix 4) add alert for compaction_rate < expected.

henry (runtime): I'll open PR for default compaction + a telemetry metric `kv_fragmentation_ratio` and a canary-run integration.

maya (oncall): handing off to runtime eng for root cause + followups. Oncall clear in 20m unless anything else flares.

ops-bot: INCIDENT update: mitigations applied. Status: degraded -> stabilizing. Next update scheduled in 30m or on escalation. :white_check_mark:

maya (oncall): tagging for postmortem: @henry @lia @sam @emily. Will attach logs and perf dumps to the incident ticket.

henry (runtime): creating incident PR with logs and proposed long-term fixes (allocator slab redesign + proactive compaction).

maya (oncall): closing thread for live triage. If anything reappears ping me directly. thanks all. :heart:
